proves.claim: a label below its minimum yields the top servable item carrying it, and none once every minimum is met.

queue.label-pick.minimum-yields-top.why: Label minimums must pull work to the labels that lack it.

proves.claim: a label at its maximum is never picked, and a closed milestone never fills a minimum.

queue.label-pick.maximum-and-closed.why: Maximums cap a label and a closed milestone must not count.

proves.claim: an item carrying a label already at its maximum is skipped, and the capped labels it carries are named.

queue.label-pick.skips-capped.why: A pin on an item whose label is full must not win over the max.

proves.claim: readGateQueueSettings reads the named file, not the machine home.

queue.settings.reads-named-file.why: A cell must not read machine settings on its own.

proves.claim: diagnostics pass background work only when every waiter knows the ordering.

queue.diagnostic.waiters-know-ordering.why: A waiter that ignores ordering can starve or reorder work.

proves.claim: every queue-cell test registered here has a stable ID and one complete record, and an unregistered test is reported and fails only with tests.registryStrict on.

queue.registry.complete.why: Without a record per test a test can be deleted or duplicated with no one noticing what it proved.

proves.claim: every queue test file that reads source files carries an input header naming the cells it reads.

queue.inputs.declared.why: A test that reads files without a header is invisible to affected-test selection and can ship a break unseen.

proves.claim: returnedFirst puts an abandoned or rework item ahead of an untouched item of the same or lower rank and keeps the original order inside each group

queue.returned.returned-items-lead-untou.why: Returned work finishes cheaper than fresh work, and held items only bounce back, so a wrong order wastes builder time.

proves.claim: returnedFirst keeps a returned item behind an untouched item of a more urgent rank

queue.returned.never-passes-a-more-urgen.why: Returned work finishes cheaper than fresh work, and held items only bounce back, so a wrong order wastes builder time.

proves.claim: returnedFirst leaves out an item whose stop reason is wall, decision or blocked

queue.returned.leaves-out-wall-decision-.why: Returned work finishes cheaper than fresh work, and held items only bounce back, so a wrong order wastes builder time.

proves.claim: missingNeeds returns the needs an agent lacks, and an empty list when it has every one

queue.needs.missing-needs-lists-what-is-.why: Needs decide which agent may take an item, so a wrong match or a misspelt need would strand work or hand it to an agent that cannot do it.

proves.claim: validateNeeds accepts only browser and gui and refuses any other name with USAGE naming the allowed list

queue.needs.validate-accepts-only-browse.why: Needs decide which agent may take an item, so a wrong match or a misspelt need would strand work or hand it to an agent that cannot do it.

proves.claim: of two submitted items that name one file, only the later-submitted one waits, on the earlier, and the earlier shows no wait for that file

queue.readiness.submitted-overlap-is-ord.why: Two submitted items waiting on each other left both unreviewed with reviewers idle.

proves.claim: an open item still waits on every claimed or submitted item that names its file

queue.readiness.open-still-waits.why: Ordering submitted items must not let an open item start on a file another item holds.

proves.claim: missingNeeds and validateNeeds imported from the queue light door are the needs module exports and give the same results.

queue.needs.light-door-exports-needs-che.why: A higher cell reaches the needs check through the queue front door, so the door must hand out the same functions.

proves.claim: routingCapacity returns readyByRoute, the ready item count per route (mid, strong), summing to readyItems and zero for a route with none

queue.logic-capacity.ready-by-route.why: The ready buffer per route needs its data before the status line and the routing policy can show or use it.

proves.claim: the readyByRoute of routingCapacity comes from the same ready list as readyItems and keeps every existing field

queue.logic-capacity.ready-by-route-real.why: The status summary calls routingCapacity, so the per-route count must come from the list it already counts.
